allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 0.6 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: mid-green leaves; brownish-purple flowers.

appearance.organs.flower.note: Its raceme drawn as one cluster that opens by the day (spec rework L1c), its kind from its characters, by the rule at the flowering plants: about 30 flowers, by eye (the Flora of North America's genus gives 10 to 150), on a raceme 2 to 3 dm long (the Burke Herbarium: 1 to 3 dm), each a greenish-purple calyx tube with four thread-like chocolate-brown petals 6 to 10 mm long curling back, and a small capsule after. From floras and extension pages as quoted in search results; the pages themselves were not read. The plant stands as tall as before: its stems end where the raceme begins.

appearance.organs.flower.inflorescence.k.note: How PlantGen lays out an inflorescence, a choice of the model's (spec rework L1): the inflorescence characters set the cluster of any look a taxon draws as one (`"inflorescence": {}`), its kind, how many units it bears on each axis, its primary branches and how it holds itself. Sizes, stalks and spacing stay set by hand until programs size their organs from characters.

appearance.organs.flower.season.note: Its days by eye from the months floras give for flowering (April to August; the Burke Herbarium: May to August), for lowland plants: buds in April, each flower open about 12 days, the raceme opening from its foot over about a month (floras give no time). Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): four thread-like petals (by hand; floras count four) between five sepals on its tubular floral cup, three stamens and a pistil of two carpels, from the characters of Saxifragaceae and Tolmiea by the rules at the flowering plants.

appearance.organs.flower.season.flower_l.note: How PlantGen draws a flower, a choice of the model's (spec rework P5): the flower characters set a flower card's perianth, its parts, how they differ by place, how far the corolla is joined into a tube, a floral cup, where the ovary sits, a resupinate flower's turn, its stamens, staminodes and carpels and its spurs. The rules also set these fields in a season's flower and bud looks that draw a flower, unless set there by hand.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a clump of long-stalked, hairy, maple-like basal leaves that sprout plantlets where blade meets stalk, with slender racemes of brownish-purple flowers. Not fitted to measurements.

generator.params.dioecious.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant bears both sexes, unless its taxa state it dioecious.

generator.params.leaves_per_node.note: What the words mean, as accounts of phyllotaxis such as Okabe and colleagues' use them: a spiral or two-ranked shoot bears one leaf at a node, a decussate one a pair and a whorled one three or more. A spiral turns about the golden angle (137.5 degrees) from node to node and two ranks half a turn; pairs and whorls alternate, each standing over the gaps of the one below, half the gap between its own leaves round (90 degrees for pairs). Three ranks turn a third of a turn, as their name says.

generator.params.sex.note: How PlantGen draws the sexes, a choice of the model's (dioecy, 2026-10-14): a plant's sex is its own draw, dealt across a package's seeds so that both sexes grow; the typical plant (sex 0.5) is female, so it shows its fruit.

generator.program.note: The lineage's own program (growth plan G2.3a), on the herb base: it gives the values its species leave unset, which the herb program gave as defaults until then.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
